status: COMPLETE AS MODEL-SELECTION SCREENING; NOT SCIENTIFICALLY VALIDATED

M1_compact_IQ_CNN.training: 15 epochs, compact 1-D CNN, raw frozen I/Q

M2_IQ_metric_prototype.training: 15 epochs, compact I/Q encoder with learned prototype head

M3_supervised_contrastive_prototype.training: 3 completed CPU epochs; screening run only because longer SupCon run exceeded available execution budget
M3_supervised_contrastive_prototype.decision: REJECT AS BACKBONE REPLACEMENT IN THIS BENCHMARK; retain as literature-informed future candidate, not a certified winner

selection_decision.selected_version_b_backbone: M0 Version-A RF recognition backbone plus new open-set/profile-security mechanisms
selection_decision.reason: No learned I/Q candidate demonstrated a credible improvement over the frozen RF control under the executed benchmark. M1 and M2 were decisively weaker; M3 screening was materially better than M1/M2 but remained below the RF baseline and was not fully trained.
selection_decision.important_boundary: This does not prove RF is globally optimal. It establishes that replacing the current RF recognition mechanism is not justified by the executed Track-A evidence. Version B therefore concentrates novelty and engineering effort on open-set security, protected adaptive profiles and poisoning resistance while retaining RF as the control recognition backbone.
selection_decision.next: Proceed directly to D8 profile evolution with strengthened open-set security, then D9 poisoning and D10 lifecycle integration.

scientific_status: Demonstrated model-selection screening; not Scientifically Validated. M3 longer-training and broader architecture sweeps may be revisited only if a concrete research question requires them, but they are not required to unblock Track-A D8-D10.
